Optimal.Notes: The 40 Hz refresh and 40 fps cap deliver a smooth, tear-free feel ideal for a racing sim; FSR upscaling from 1024x640 recovers sharpness while keeping frametimes consistent. A good all-round profile for solo racing sessions.

profiles.Summary: Assetto Corsa is a 2014 DirectX 11 racing simulation that runs on Proton with a gold rating, meaning most players get it working with some tweaking. The Steam Deck's RDNA 2 GPU sits comfortably above the minimum spec, so stable 40–60 fps is achievable at low-to-medium settings, though the game's Windows-only nature and lack of official controller support may require some initial setup.
profiles.BasisNote: No specific Steam Deck player reports were available; profiles are estimated from the PC minimum/recommended requirements, the Deck's RDNA 2 GPU capability, and the ProtonDB gold rating. On your first run, check frame pacing on a busy track with a full grid and drop to the Optimal or MaxBattery profile if frame rate is unstable.

MaxBattery.Notes: Render at 960x600 with FSR upscaling to keep the GPU relaxed; a 7 W TDP cap and 900 MHz GPU clock hold steady 30 fps and maximise play time. Use Steam Input to map gamepad controls before launching.

KnownIssues: No native controller/gamepad mapping — requires manual Steam Input configuration or in-game axis binding before the car is drivable.
Game is DirectX 11 only and may require Proton Experimental or GE-Proton for best compatibility; some users report needing to set a specific Proton version to avoid crashes at launch.
The in-game launcher (AC Launcher) can fail to open properly under Proton — launching directly via Steam's target executable workaround or using GE-Proton is commonly needed.
Online multiplayer may have issues under Proton; single-player and offline modes are generally the most stable path on Deck.

MaxPerformance.Notes: Native 1280x800 with high detail targets 60 fps; expect occasional dips to the low 50s on busy circuits with many cars. This profile drains the battery quickly, so best used plugged in or for short sessions.

Optimal.Notes: A 45 fps cap at 90 Hz gives smooth, responsive racing with a good visual balance. FSR upscaling from 1024x640 recovers GPU headroom while keeping the image sharp enough on the OLED panel.
